speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (also known as Suboptimal Intake Jaundice).

The clinical picture of a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (total 16.1 mg/dL, direct normal) and a weight gain of only ~134g over two weeks is classic for insufficient milk intake. Although breastfeeding is occurring, the frequency or effectiveness of feeding is likely inadequate, leading to dehydration and reduced stooling, which prevents bilirubin excretion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice.
